concepts.def: Artificial lakes that store water, e.g. Kielder Water in Northumberland.
Pipelines or canals move water from surplus to deficit regions.
Removing salt from seawater; energy-intensive but reliable.
Reducing demand via metering, low-flow taps and education.
Low-cost, local schemes like hand-dug wells and rope pumps.
Reused household water from sinks and showers for non-drinking uses. 🚿

walkthroughs.body_html:
Reservoirs store winter rainfall.

Kielder Water in NE England holds up to 200 billion litres.

It supplies homes and industry across the region.

Water transfers move surplus around.

UK plans include a proposed Severn-Thames transfer to support the dry South East.

Big projects can disrupt habitats and cost a lot to build.

Low-cost intermediate technology works in LICs.

Charity-built wells and rope pumps are cheap, repairable and locally owned.

They cut walking time and disease.
